title: Allow profile ordering in settings
purpose: Persist user selected profile list order

files.previous_behavior: Profiles were displayed in stored insertion order without reorder controls.
files.new_behavior: Valid up/down moves reorder existing profile objects, save profiles.json and refresh consumers; invalid moves are ignored.
files.data_impact: Reorders Items in existing profiles.json on user action; no schema or credential changes.
files.access_control_impact: none: existing trusted chrome message routing and profile permissions remain unchanged.
risks: SaveProfiles retains its existing silent IO failure behavior.
files.rollback: Revert this commit and rebuild; existing profiles.json remains compatible and preserves its last saved order.

files.purpose: Expose profile ordering controls in settings.
files.previous_behavior: Profiles were displayed in stored insertion order without reorder controls.
files.new_behavior: Each profile has accessible up/down buttons; boundary buttons are disabled and clicks send prof.move.
files.data_impact: Sends profile id and direction only; no credential writes.
files.access_control_impact: none: existing trusted chrome message routing and profile permissions remain unchanged.
risks: Additional buttons increase profile header width on narrow settings panels.
files.rollback: Revert this commit and rebuild; existing profiles.json remains compatible and preserves its last saved order.

production_safety.operational_data: No operational profile or credential data read or changed during development.
production_safety.schema_migration: none: existing list order is used without new fields.
external_side_effects: Local build artifact in native/publish-profile-order; running application unchanged.

verification.evidence: Zero errors; existing MSB3277 WindowsBase dependency warning.

verification.command: dotnet publish native/native.csproj -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained true -p:PublishSingleFile=true -o native/publish-profile-order -v quiet
node --check --input-type=commonjs (all embedded chrome.html scripts via UTF-8 stdin)

residual_risks: Live interaction and restart persistence not exercised against user data; running app still uses previous executable.
Existing silent save failure behavior remains.
